name: Autodesk Revit
tagline: BIM software for designing and documenting buildings and infrastructure in 3D.
bestFor: BIM teams at architecture and engineering firms
description: Revit is Autodesk's BIM application for modelling buildings with parametric walls, doors and windows, then producing sheets and schedules from that model. It is sold by subscription per user or through Autodesk's token-based Flex plan, and it runs on Windows only.
pros: Parametric BIM model with schedules and sheet documentation
Imports and exports IFC, 3DM, SKP, OBJ and STEP
Worksharing on a central model, plus Dynamo and an API for automation
cons: Windows only; Mac users need a virtual machine or dual boot
Subscription only, at $3,005 a year per user
Free licences are for verified students and educators only

plans.name: Revit subscription
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $3,005. 3-year term $9,020. Pay-as-you-go Flex from $99 for 33 tokens (Revit uses 10 tokens a day).

integrations: Twinmotion for Revit, Dynamo, Autodesk Forma, Autodesk App Store; IFC, 3DM, SKP, OBJ, STEP

name: Graphisoft Archicad
tagline: BIM software for architects that runs on both Windows and macOS.
bestFor: Architects who want BIM on Mac or Windows
description: Archicad is Graphisoft's BIM application for modelling, documenting and visualising buildings, and it runs natively on Windows and macOS. It is sold per seat in three subscription tiers, Studio, Collaborate and Max, which differ in teamwork hosting, MEP tools, add-ons and AI credits.
pros: Runs natively on both Windows and macOS
Imports and exports IFC and DWG
Higher tiers include cloud teamwork (BIMcloud SaaS) and MEP Designer
cons: New commercial licences are subscription only
Studio's teamwork uses self-hosted BIMcloud Basic, not the cloud service
Free EDU licences are watermarked and cannot be used commercially

plans.name: Archicad Studio
plans.notes: Per seat, plus tax, billed yearly at $2,414. Includes BIMcloud Basic (self-hosted) and BIMx Pro Baseline; no MEP Designer.

plans.name: Archicad Collaborate
plans.notes: Per seat, plus tax, billed yearly at $2,840. Adds BIMcloud SaaS, MEP Designer and the ProKit Suite.

plans.name: Archicad Max
plans.notes: Per seat, plus tax, billed yearly at $5,700. Adds all language versions and more AI credits.

integrations: BIMcloud, BIMx, MEP Designer, Autodesk Forma connection (Collaborate and up)

name: Vectorworks Architect
tagline: 2D drafting, 3D modelling and BIM software for architects in one application.
bestFor: Design-led practices mixing 2D drafting and BIM
description: Vectorworks Architect combines 2D drafting, 3D modelling on the Parasolid engine, and BIM with openBIM and IFC support. It is sold as a monthly or annual subscription from the Vectorworks online store.
pros: Lower annual price than Revit or Archicad
Supports openBIM and IFC, with links to Revit, SketchUp and Rhino
cons: The US store sells subscriptions only
Trial length is not stated on the vendor page
Monthly billing costs $510 a year more than annual

plans.name: Architect
plans.notes: Per licence (one user), billed yearly at $1,530 (US store).

plans.name: Design Suite
plans.notes: Per licence, billed yearly at $1,980. Includes Architect, Landmark and Spotlight.

integrations: Revit, SketchUp, Rhino, Photoshop, Cinema 4D, Maxon Redshift

name: AutoCAD (Architecture toolset)
tagline: Autodesk's 2D and 3D CAD software, with an Architecture toolset included in the subscription.
description: An AutoCAD subscription includes AutoCAD for Windows and Mac, AutoCAD Web, and seven industry toolsets, one of which is the Architecture toolset. The toolsets run on Windows only.
pros: DWG is the native file format
All seven toolsets, including Architecture, come with every subscription
One subscription covers Windows, Mac and web
cons: The Architecture toolset is Windows only
Not a full BIM tool like Revit

plans.name: AutoCAD subscription
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $2,095. 3-year term $6,285. Includes the Architecture toolset and six others (Windows only). Flex tokens also available.

platforms: Mac (base AutoCAD only, no Architecture toolset)
integrations: AutoCAD Web and mobile, Autodesk App Store

name: Chief Architect Premier
tagline: Residential design software that builds walls, roofs and framing automatically from floor plans.
description: Chief Architect Premier is home design software whose automatic building tools generate walls, floors, roofs and framing as a model evolves, with GPU ray-traced rendering built in. It is sold by monthly or annual subscription, and one licence runs on either Windows or macOS.
pros: Automatic framing, roofs and building tools aimed at residential work
Built-in rendering with GPU ray tracing
One licence runs natively on Windows or Mac
cons: IFC is not listed among its import and export formats
Needs an internet connection every 14 days for licence checks
trial: Free trial (printing, saving and exporting disabled)

plans.name: Premier
plans.notes: Per licence, billed yearly at $1,995. Includes upgrades, premium catalogs and priority support.

integrations: Chief As-Built app, 3D Viewer app; DWG/DXF, SKP, OBJ import
